This feels like an Adult Swim short (derogatory). Rango has an instantly compelling premise, but too bad its execution is everything I do not want from a premise as delightfully absurd as a hero's journey from cowardly Lizard to Clint Eastwood. It's so painfully self aware and satirical of everything that it just loses the magic that it could have had. Rango is much more of a comedy than an adventure, a Western or a drama, and it sucks that this is the approach they went for. You are absolutely not supposed to watch Once Upon A Time In The West before this, because most of the elements in this film that make you go "oh shit, that's actually really cool" is just stripped from that one. I don't even like Leone or that movie that much for the matter, but I genuinely checked out once the literal main theme song is just a lackluster spoof of Man With A Harmonica. So many shots are just ripped from Leone without even any interesting remixing of ideas like what Tarantino usually does, just homage for the sake of homage. The movie itself also does not hold up on its own. Rango is supposed to be flawed, but he's so fucking irritatingly incompetent and genuinely idiotic that it makes me completely unable to root for his character. He's not a likeable loser or a charming asshole, he's just that one annoying kid in school that you lowkey understand why they're bullied. And all the characters are just whatever, Beans is the only character that I actually find kinda sweet, too bad she's just the damsel in distress. The movie also feels really really long. Could have ended like 15 minutes before if we got rid of all the shitty Leone homages and trimmed one unnecessary set piece. The animation is pretty gorgeous though, that I can't lie. It's too bad so much of it has to be a homage of Leone that it lacks originality. That (SPOILER) character appearing to Rango before the final act is a little tacky, but it's pretty cute. Puts a smile on my face.

I remember really wanting to see this when it released (though in my memory it released way earlier than it did in reality). I remember so many people singing its praises. I saved Rango for a long time, as I have with a lot of these more mainstream-but-beloved movies. As is often the case, it really has nothing going for it without nostalgia backing it up. Often looking really good, Rango opens pretty strong with a string of whacky cartoon slapstick setpieces, then it completely runs out of steam when it drops into the most generic American family, action/comedy movie template story and just plods through it with nothing memorable, no real characters, no real personality. The character designs are fun. I ended up having to pause it and return 24 hours later because it was boring me to death. I don't think a family comedy should be capable of being boring, but it's so completely lacking in an identity of it's own that there's nothing to connect to. The acid-western epiphany sequence towards the end shakes some energy into the film, by presenting the act of walking into traffic as the solution to all of your problems in a film primarily for children... And of course the epiphany is that capitalism and greed are wasting resources and destroying the earth, which is never really engaged with at all and then Rango wastes loads of water and causes massive amounts of damage and is basically bailed out by everyone else, as he is for the entire story, leaving there with pretty much nothing of value by the end. I guess the Johnny Depp mania of the era was hard carrying this thing.

Hmm muistin että tää olis ollu parempi... ei siis täysin huono mutta paljon asioita joista en pitänyt. Sekava, poukkoileva ja mitäänsanomaton tarina, unohdettavat hahmot ja todella, TODELLA pakotettua huumoria etenkin ensimmäisellä puoliskolla. Siis oikeasti, tuntui että yhden yhtä asiaa ei oteta leffan ekalla puolikkaalla tosissaan ja joka ikinen lause tuplataan jollain vitsillä, gagilla tai hassuttelulla. Ihan saatanan raivostuttavaa. Lisäksi tuo Rango hahmona on niin perseestä todella pitkään, että kun loppupuolella vihdoin jotain kauan odotettua hahmokehitystä tapahtuu, ei se ilmene mitenkään uskottavana. Onneksi jälkipuoli leffasta on ylipäätään parempi ja vakavampi sävyltään. Olisi ollut sitä alusta asti ja huumoria siroteltuna sinne tänne, niin tässä olisi ollut potentiaalia. Tuntui nyt siltä, että ne vaan tyhjensi jonkun kuratoimattoman vitsivihkosensa vaan sarjatulella, ja sitten muisti että ainiin tässä pitää joku juonikin tehdä ja ohoh meillähän olis tässä ihan hyviäkin aineksia joita vois käyttää. Sinänsä harmi, koska animaatiotyyli on hyvin ainutlaatuinen ja mieleenpainuva, ja moni visuaalinen ja esteettinen ratkaisu on todella osuvia. Ja OSA huumorista on oikein hauskaakin, tai olisi hauskaa jos sille antaisi tilaa vaikuttaa. Sinänsä idea tämmöisestä "aikuisten" animaatiosta, jossa on paljon kaksimielisiä vitsejä ja sivistyssanoja, ja melkoisen rujo animaatiotyyli, on todela hyvä ja toimisi, jos siihen uskallettaisiin nojata sellaisenaan. Nyt tämä tuntuu pokkuroinnilta lasten hömppäelokuvan ja vakavasti otettavan aikuisten leffan välillä, eikä tee kumpaakaan hääppöisesti.

Animated films are something I’d like to spend more time diving into as I go deeper into cinema. I’ve watched a good portion of the acclaimed and popular animated films over the years, and this is one that I’ve seen a long time ago. Johnny Depp’s performance as Rango is a good one for sure. He does a good job of portraying a character that almost ironically treats his life as a performance in itself. Rattlesnake Jake is one of the best animated villains in any Disney or Pixar style film I’ve ever seen, and even though he’s not in the film until the last half hour or so, it is worth the wait. I enjoy the camaraderie that the various residents of Dirt manage to develop over the troubling events that the story focuses on. Nicely timed comedic relief is a focal point here, as with most films of this genre, and doesn’t take away from the progression or characters. Overall, if you have the right expectations, it’s a fun watch if nothing else. I enjoy the western style influence and setting, and wish more animated films shared this time period.

J'aime beaucoup la DA qui représente bien le côté crade des habitants, façon animaux du désert sèche bien Americain. Bien détaillés, tous avec du vécu de par leurs séquelles physiques ou même psychologiques. Le rendu Western est franchement bien retranscrit, bien animé et détaillé, ce côté vide du désert qui donne franchement soif à regarder. Avec tous les codes du Western : des habitants hostiles, des pilleurs, Shérif et autres bandits au sein du village. C'est clairement le gros point que je lui donne. Ensuite, personnage assez sympathique, clairement en proie à une belle aventure, et cela le montre bien avec ce côté rêveur de quand il était encore domestiqué. Son côté maladroit, peut-être égoïste de par certains de ses choix, s'inventant un nom et une histoire pour mieux s'intégrer. Tout un passage où il paraît crédible aux yeux des autres, le rendant moins héroïque qu'il en a l'air. Mais sans compter son évolution qui résume parfaitement son caractère qui met en défaut ce qu'il devrait être : s'assumer et se construire de lui-même au lieu de mentir constamment. D'ailleurs, représentation assez rigolote pour ceux qui l'auront reconnue à ce passage, vous verrez. J'aime beaucoup tout l'enjeu concernant leur ressource de survie qu'est l'eau. Comment cela devient rare, ce qui peut créer des conflits, d'autres leaders peuvent jouer là-dessus pour asseoir leur pouvoir, et cela nous aura valu un antagoniste assez bien trouvé dans la créativité, d'animal reconnaissable et aux allures bien Western avec son arme au bout de la queue. Un bel aura, une vraie présence qui vole limite la vedette à l'autre premier antagoniste qui est plus affaires et leader. Bon, j'ai quand même eu un vrai enjeu pour suivre le film au vu d'une fatigue qui commençait à monter, ce qui fait que j'ai eu quelques passages qui donnent l'impression d'être longs et ennuyants, mais c'était peut-être moi. Cela va évidemment influencer ma note finale concernant mon expérience personnel, mais pas grave, j'assume mes responsabilités en termes de visionnage où je dois me stopper si je sens une once d'assoupissement. Mais bon, au moins le film a de bons gags, le message final est correct, et les enjeux de sécheresse parfaitement expliqués. Film sympa, sans être exceptionnel. Juste dommage que je trouve la BO assez mémorable.

Depp's improv is much less charming these days than it was 15 years ago, and it's got probably the worst example of the dreaded "liar revealed" trope in recent memory. But it is also one of the most artistically creative and visually impressive pieces of animation ever put to screen. It's more than just "pretty". Animation just being pretty doesn't excuse flawed writing, but the level of artistic talent and creativity put into this film is different from "pretty"

He starts as a chameleon in a tank, gets thrown in the middle of no where, fakes it til he makes it, becomes sheriff and starts proving it through moments such as standing up to Rattlesnake Jake and protecting Dirt. He ends up becoming a symbol of hope and a true hero for Dirt. The Wild West theme and the presentation of this film are amazing. The pretty sunsets and night skies, the desert setting, a great score, the sounds such as the clock hitting high noon on a Wednesday or guns reloading, and the town of Dirt give it a distinct feel. The Mariachi owls as narrators and occasionally breaking the fourth wall also added on to its feel. Rango is a really fun film with a great protagonist who goes from zero to hero. Combine that with comedy and a beautiful yet distinct Wild West presentation makes this a great watch. 8/10

Deconstruye la típica trama del viaje del héroe con un protagonista carismático que debe volverse más fuerte para encontrar su propio camino. Aparte como dato está es la primera película que vi en el cine en toda mi vida, con tan solo tres años, y me ha encantado poder revivirla ahora de mayor.

“No man can walk out on his own story.” Rango is a love letter to the classic westerns of the 20th century while simultaneously being one of the greatest westerns of the 21st century. It somehow manages to follow the classic western blueprint step by step while checking off every single trope along the way, and yet there is nothing else like it. I adore Rango. The team behind this project were very clearly firing on all cylinders. The script is sharp, the plot is tight, the visuals are incredible and the voice cast is perfect. It’s just a start to finish treat of a film. There are some truly inspiring scenes in this movie. There are plenty of gags and fun throughout, but there are also several moments where it gets incredibly thoughtful, philosophical and emotional. It has to be one of my favorite animated movies at this point. Every time I revisit it I walk away with a stronger love and appreciation for it. The design for Rattlesnake Jake is S tier. The designs for every creature are incredible but the scene when Rattlesnake Jake shows up is genuinely intense.

La vi hace mucho tiempo de niño, al inicio no me parecía la gran cosa, solo veía bichos feos y una lagartija vaquera. Al crecer, por los azares del destino, la quise ver. No recuerdo el cómo ni el porqué. Ahora Rango, una película que para mí se ha ganado un lugar preciado en mi corazón. El personaje es un cobarde con aires de grandeza, quien habla mucho y actúa poco. Ha fingido ser más fuerte o seguro de lo que realmente es; pero aun así, acepta su destino. Un hombre (lagartija, creo) que está dispuesto a entregarse al espectáculo de la vida y ser el personaje principal de su propio destino. Rango empieza actuando en un terrario y termina actuando en el mundo real, hasta que la actuación se vuelve su realidad. Para mí, creo que de eso se trata un poco la vida: fingir lo que queremos ser para reconfortarnos un poco y darnos esos pequeños empujones que necesitamos en el camino. No puede evitar verme reflejado; es cine absoluto.
